THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

Herb-Garlic Pork Chops + Cowboy Butter Drizzle

Restaurant-grade weeknight in 30 minutes. Herb marinade carries the chop, Parmesan-Stravecchio crusted snap peas eat like a craveable side (not the leftover compartment), and the Cowboy Butter Drizzle is the macro reframe — Laughing Cow Light + bone broth + aged Parm replace 4 tbsp of butter for ~75 cal per 2 tbsp instead of ~200.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME30 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~450 cal | ~50g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: PAT + DRY 1-2 HOURS AHEAD IF YOU CAN. Pork chops on a rack in the fridge uncovered. Surface dry = real sear. Wet pork = steam + sadness.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 4 boneless pork loin chops, 1-inch thick (~6 oz each = 24 oz total)

SNAP PEAS (shared — kid + adult eat the same)

  • 2 cups fresh sugar snap peas, trimmed
  • Olive oil spray
  • 2 tbsp food-processed Kirkland Parmigiano Stravecchio (from a wedge)
  • 4 tbsp crushed Corn Chex (pulse in food processor)
  • Pinch salt + black pepper

ADULT SAUCE FOLD-INS (added AT THE END to the adult portion only)

  • 2 tbsp fresh parsley, finely chopped
  • 1 tbsp fresh chives, finely chopped
  • Extra chili flakes (to taste)
  • Full Cowboy Butter recipe (cross-link → )

MARINADE

  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 8 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tbsp Kikkoman All-Purpose Soy Sauce
  • 1 tbsp Lea & Perrins Worcestershire Sauce
  • 1 tbsp Smash Kitchen Dijon Mustard
  • 1.5 tbsp fresh rosemary, finely chopped
  • 1.5 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
  • 1.5 tsp smoked paprika
  • 1 tsp chili flakes
  • 1 tsp black pepper
  • 1 tsp salt
  • 1 lemon, juiced

Option 1

  • Plain Cowboy Butter (1/3 of the batch, set aside BEFORE folding in herbs)

Allergens: dairy, soy, fish.

AFTER COOKING. Same marinade, same sear, same peas, same Cowboy Butter base. The split happens at PLATING + at the sauce fold (parsley + chives + chili flakes into the adult half only).

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.PAT + DRY (if time). Chops on a rack in the fridge uncovered for 1-2 hr. Surface dry = real sear.
  2. 2.MARINATE. Whisk all marinade ingredients in a large bowl. Add chops, flip to coat. 30 min min, 2 hr ideal.
  3. 3.PREP THE CRUST. Food-process 2 oz Kirkland Parmigiano Stravecchio into coarse grated. Pulse 4 tbsp Corn Chex in the same processor into coarse crumbs.
  4. 4.PREHEAT OVEN 425°F. Toss snap peas with oil spray + Parm + crushed Chex + salt in a bowl, then spread on parchment-lined sheet pan.
  5. 5.BAKE PEAS. 18-22 min until deep golden + crispy edges.
  6. 6.SEAR THE CHOPS. Stainless or cast iron, medium-HIGH, 2 tsp oil. Lay chops away from you, DON'T MOVE for 4 min. Flip once. 3-4 min side 2. Pull at internal 145°F. Rest 5 min.

Adult — Sliced Chop + Herb-Forward Cowboy Butter

  1. 7.SLICE THE CHOP. 1 chop per adult, sliced thin across the grain.
  2. 8.PLATE. Sliced chop over crusted snap peas in a wide bowl. Drizzle adult Cowboy Butter (the parsley + chives + chili flakes one) cross-hatched over the top. DON'T POUR — the pattern is the visual.

Kid — Diced Chop + Plain Cowboy Butter Dip · Option 1

  1. 7.DICE 1/2 CHOP per kid into 1/2-inch cubes. Trim off the heaviest char if your kid rejects visible burn.
  2. 8.PLATE INTO 3-COMPARTMENT TRAY. Diced chop in compartment 1, crusted snap peas in compartment 2, plain Cowboy Butter (the 1/3 you pulled before the herb fold) in the dip well.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Sliced Chop + Herb-Forward Cowboy Butter: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Diced Chop + Plain Cowboy Butter Dip: Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • MARINATE 30 MIN MINIMUM. Whisk 2 tbsp olive oil + 8 minced garlic cloves + 2 tbsp soy + 1 tbsp Worcestershire + 1 tbsp Dijon + 1.5 tbsp chopped rosemary + 1.5 tbsp chopped thyme + 1.5 tsp smoked paprika + 1 tsp chili flakes + 1 tsp salt + 1 tsp pepper + juice of 1 lemon. Add chops, flip to coat both sides. 30 min minimum, 2 hr ideal.
  • PARALLEL COOK. While chops marinate (or while pan heats): food-process 2 oz Kirkland Stravecchio into coarse grated. Pulse 4 tbsp Corn Chex in the same processor (or zip-bag + roll) into coarse crumbs.

If something fails

Chops came out pale + steamy, no sear: Wet pork OR overcrowded pan OR pan not hot enough. Pat dry. Don't crowd. Pan should sizzle aggressively when chops touch — if it whispers, wait longer.

Chops dry + tough: Overcooked. Pull at internal 145°F (USDA safe — pork can be slightly pink). Rest 5 min for juices to redistribute. Or buy thicker chops (1.5 inch) — they're more forgiving than thin.

Snap pea coating fell off / didn't adhere: Not enough oil OR you didn't toss before spreading. Spray more, toss in a bowl first, THEN spread on parchment. Pre-tossing always beats sprinkling on the sheet pan.

Cowboy Butter curdled / grainy: Heat too high when whisking in Laughing Cow. LOW heat only — the wedges need to melt slowly. If already curdled, stir in 1 tbsp cold bone broth + whisk hard; sometimes it re-emulsifies.

Adult sauce parsley turned gray by the time we ate: You folded too early or the sauce was too hot. Fold parsley + chives AT THE END, after the sauce is off heat and slightly cooled. Or sprinkle them on top at the table.

Kid sauce too cheesy / strong for the kid: Thin the kid portion with 1 more tbsp bone broth. Or sub 1 tbsp plain Greek yogurt for a milder kid version — same color, half the intensity.

Chops + peas finished at different times: Peas need 18-22 min at 425°F. Chops need 8-10 min total + 5 min rest. Start peas FIRST, then sear chops after 10 min of pea bake. They land together.

Storage and reheating

Store: Pork chops hold 3 days. Snap peas best fresh (soften in fridge) — Day 2 is OK; Day 3 they're soggy. Cowboy Butter holds 5 days in a jar (re-warm gently before serving).

Reheat: Pork chops: cast iron 60-90 sec per side OR 350°F oven 5 min. Don't microwave — rubberizes the crust. Snap peas: air fryer 4 min at 400°F to re-crisp. Cowboy Butter: low-heat saucepan + 1 tbsp bone broth splash to loosen.

Lasts: Best Day 1. Acceptable Day 2-3 with re-crisping. Don't freeze — Laughing Cow breaks on thaw.

Make this when

You want a real plated dinner — not a wrap, not a bowl, an actual sliced pork chop with crispy snap peas and a creamy drizzle. Adults get the full chop sliced thin with the herb-flecked Cowboy Butter on top. Kids get diced chunks in a 3-compartment tray + cream sauce in the dip well (sauce stays plain — no herb flecks, no chili flakes).

Brands I use

Kirkland Signature
Parmigiano Reggiano Stravecchio (aged over 36 months, ~2 lb wedge)
Real aged Parm with the salt crystals + nutty depth that survive oven roasting. Pre-grated tubs disappear into the dish — you'd taste them as 'cheesy crumb' instead of 'aged Parm crunch'. Costco's best cheese deal.
Laughing Cow
Light Creamy Swiss Wedges (6 oz / 8 wedges)
The macro lever in Cowboy Butter. 3 wedges replace ~4 tbsp butter for 1/4 the fat. Spreadable when cold, melts smooth when warm. 35 cal per wedge.
Lea & Perrins
The Original Worcestershire Sauce (10 oz)
Molasses + tamarind + anchovy umami. Used in BOTH the marinade (1 tbsp) AND the Cowboy Butter (1/2 tsp). The brand specifically because L&P has the right balance — store-brand Worcestershire is often watery.
General Mills
Corn Chex Cereal (12 oz, gluten-free)
4 tbsp pulsed to coarse crumbs = the snap pea crunch. Gluten-free, neutral flavor, lighter than panko, more flavor than rice crisps. The 2:1 chex-to-Parm ratio is the move — more crunch, less density.
Smash Kitchen
Dijon Mustard
1 tbsp in marinade + 1 tsp in Cowboy Butter. Same brand both places. Sharp + clean.
Kikkoman
All-Purpose Soy Sauce
2 tbsp in the marinade. Clean salt + umami. Default soy on this site — cross-recipe with TKS Sauce (id 35), Lift Drizzle, Lettuce Wraps (id 38).
Kirkland
Chicken Bone Broth
4 tbsp in Cowboy Butter — adds body without dairy. Beef bone broth also works (richer). Cross-recipe with id 24, id 31, Lift Drizzle.
Kirkland
Sweet Cream Butter (unsalted)
Just 1 tsp in the Cowboy Butter — bloom the garlic + paprika. Most of the 'butter' work is done by the Laughing Cow swap; the small pat of real butter gives the dish the cowboy-butter aroma.
